newsitem.title: UK: Petronas says to buy up to six more LNG tankers.
newsitem.headline: Petronas says to buy up to six more LNG tankers.

text.p: Malaysia's state-owned oil company, Petronas will finalise plans to acquire another four to six liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers by early next year, OPEC news agency OPECNA said on Tuesday.

It quoted the Malaysian news agency Bernama reporting Petronas senior vice president for corporate planning and development, Hamzah Bakar, saying the company has received tenders from several shipyards in France and Japan to build the tankers.
He was speaking aboard the Puteri Firus, Petronas' fifth recently delivered LNG tanker built by French shipyard Chantiers de l'Atlantique.
The $280 million tanker, capable of carrying 130,294 tonnes of LNG, will cater for Petronas' customers in Japan, Taiwan and South Korea.
Hamzah said more tankers would be required to meet the increasing transportation needs of the LNG industry, particularly after the completion of a third LNG plant in Bintulu.
Completion of the $6 billion plant by the year 2001 will make Malaysia the world's largest LNG producer with total output of about 23 million tonnes a year.
